recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Any desire for stronger public design prose saying identifier cardinality should generally be repeating should be handled as a new editorial/design issue, not as a late source edit for this already-applied Published issue.
issue_request: FHIR-5666 requested broad consistency for .identifier cardinality and type across several DSTU1 resources. Its Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution specifically applied Observation.identifier and DiagnosticReport.identifier as 0..* Identifier, noted a Substance preapplication, and recorded MnM tooling/design guidance rather than applying every originally listed resource change.
initial_application: Commit 301f09fdfe applied the Observation portion by changing Observation.identifier from 0..1 to 0..* and adding a #5666 committee note in the old spreadsheet. Commit 6a069aa5ab preapplied the Substance identifier changes in response to a build warning. Later source refactors, including the 2021 StructureDefinition conversion, carried the applied Observation and Substance state into current XML source.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini shows the current active resources and lists DeviceObservationReport, Query, Supply, and SecurityEvent as removed resources. Current active listed resources with top-level identifier elements use type Identifier and max=*, including Observation and DiagnosticReport. MessageHeader has no top-level identifier and only a response identifier constrained to 1..1 Identifier, consistent with the Jira discussion and the modified resolution. AuditEvent has no identifier, matching the Jira comment that the SecurityEvent/AuditEvent part was removed because no application was found. Current Resource notes cover consistent business identifiers, and suppressed build messages show the identifier-warning surface still exists.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The conformance-impacting current source already has Observation.identifier and DiagnosticReport.identifier as 0..* Identifier and does not contain a current-build stale identifier type/cardinality error traceable to FHIR-5666.
